calls.head: Anaheim pounces on mistakes, and Edmonton makes them
calls.body: Anaheim ranks 3rd of 32 for chances off turnovers (7.7% of its chances come right after winning the puck); Edmonton ranks 29th for avoiding breakdowns.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: 0.4% of Anaheim’s 5-on-5 chances came right after winning the puck, against its usual 7.7%.

calls.head: Quality over quantity for Edmonton
calls.body: Anaheim has struggled to keep shots to the perimeter (26th of 32), and Edmonton makes its shots count: one expected goal for every 15.3 unblocked shots, 10th in the league.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: Edmonton needed 13.4 unblocked shots per expected goal, against its usual 15.3.

ANA.head: We had this close to even (49% for Anaheim), and it went Edmonton’s way.

EDM.head: We had this close to even (51% for Edmonton), and Edmonton came through.

surprises.head: Edmonton won without the better chances
surprises.body: Expected goals favoured Anaheim, 3.2 to 2.6, with empty nets left out. D. Levi stopped 1.2 more goals than expected.

surprises.head: Anaheim shot far more than usual
surprises.body: 75.5 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5, adjusted for score and venue, against its usual 59.8.

surprises.head: Edmonton tried a different line
surprises.body: I. Howard, J. Samanski, M. Jones played 5:31 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Edmonton’s usual lines.
